32-bit versions still do have a limit of 4 GB of memory per process (even though different processes can use a total of more than 4 GB).
Per application you still end up with a 4 GB limit. But 2 processes can run in 2 separate 4 GB if you have 8GB installed.

You can use a PAE kernel to address more than 4GB RAM on a 32-bit machine (it will access up to 64GB). It's inefficient and the only real use-case for it is Socket 603/604 Xeons.
